exposure: Single oral doses of vitamin A (0, 25,000, 50,000, or 200,000 IU VA)
cohort: Male and female newborn piglets (n = 313) born from sows fed a vitamin A-free diet, who received varying oral doses of vitamin A within 12 hours of birth.
finding: Single high-dose vitamin A supplementation in newborn piglets was well absorbed and stored dose-dependently in tissues, but extrahepatic tissue levels and serum concentrations showed transient enhancement, and vitamin A-deficient piglets surprisingly gained more weight by 240 hours.
